title: Ernie Wilkins and Joe Williams' Every Day revive Basie
summary: They sort out who arranged Every Day and credit Wilkins and Joe Williams for Basie's popularity returning.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: Which one -- Frank Foster did "Every Day," didn't he? I think.
Oh, was it? Well, Frank Foster did the one on the back, "The Comeback," which was practically as good.
Yeah, sure. And then Ernie Wilkins did (HUMMING) -- oh, I can't think of it.* We played it last night. He did that and, oh, he did such fantastic -- Ernie did a lot of --
Yeah, that's true. I shouldn't overlook him, because --
Ernie Wilkins played a big part in Basie's *"Shiny Stockings."
Sure, he did. But after Joe Williams made "Every Day," and "Smack Dab in the Middle," and all those blues things, then Basie became -- it was a new Basie band. So his popularity soared again.
